description: All release-age policy lives here, and this preset is extended LAST in renovate.json for that
reason. minimumReleaseAge is a plain scalar, so the last matching rule wins; the two rules
below that remove a soak have to beat every earlier setter, including the 1/7/30-day
per-update-type ladder in github>ppat/renovate-presets and override-calver's flat 14 days.
Keep this entry last in extends, and keep new release-age rules in this file rather than
somewhere earlier where an unrelated preset can silently outrank them.

packageRules.description: delay patch updates to 7 days (from 1 day)
delay minor updates to 30 days (from 7 days)

description: Images this repo builds itself (docker.io/ppatlabs/*) are adopted as soon as they are
published: no release-age soak, on any update type. PROBLEM: a soak exists to let someone
ELSE's release be found broken by someone else before this cluster takes it. For an image
we build there is no such someone else -- the build is ours, it has already passed its own
repo's CI, and the soak only delays our own change from reaching the cluster. This is not
a claim that first-party images are safer or better tested than upstream ones; it is that
the thing a soak waits for does not exist for them.
No matchUpdateTypes, deliberately: version updates and digest refreshes alike, major
included. Enumerating types would leave whichever type was not listed soaked by whatever
set it last -- the 1/7/30-day per-update-type ladder from github>ppat/renovate-presets for
obsidian and obsidian-tools, override-calver's flat 14 days for openclaw -- and a soak
under internalChecksFilter 'strict' is a suppressed branch, not a late PR (see the digest
rule below for that mechanism).
'minimumReleaseAge: null' is a workaround spelling, not a semantic assertion: null is the
unset value, and checkMinimumReleaseAge (util/minimum-release-age.ts) skips the check when
the value is falsy. Read it as 'zero'; Renovate has no literal zero for this option.
Both spellings of the name are listed: the registry-prefixed form the kubernetes manager
emits for the image reference AS WRITTEN in the manifest (docker.io/ppatlabs/<name>), and
the bare form a '# renovate: datasource=docker depName=...' annotation would produce. A
matcher that matches nothing raises no error -- 'ppatlabs/{/,}**' was inert for two years
for exactly that reason (#3795). Note the idiom takes NO slash before the brace.
A digest refresh on a container image is never soaked. PROBLEM: a digest update means the
tag this repo ALREADY runs was repointed upstream at a rebuilt image. The version decision
was taken when the tag was adopted; soaking the refresh does not defer adopting something
new, it keeps the cluster on a build the publisher has already replaced -- usually a
rebuild for a CVE in a base layer, which is the last thing to sit on.
And it does not merely delay it. Renovate ages a digest update against the newest matching
version's timestamp (lookup/index.ts applyMinimumReleaseAgeToDigestUpdate, which re-runs
applyPackageRules with updateType set -- that is why an update-type-matched rule reaches it
at all), and for a MUTABLE tag that timestamp is the moment upstream last repointed it. So
every rebuild restarts the clock: an image rebuilt more often than the soak is long can
never clear it. With this repo's internalChecksFilter 'strict' the held update is not a
late PR either -- it is stamped pendingChecks:true and the branch is never created
(update/branch/index.js, 'creation is disabled because internalChecksFilter was not met').
No error, no PR, nothing to notice. Observed on live 44.30.4:
ghcr.io/home-operations/home-assistant's digest refresh came back pendingChecks:true under
override-calver's 14-day soak and pendingChecks:false with this rule, everything else
equal. Its mechanism is the second, harsher one: that tag resolves NO releaseTimestamp at
all, and Renovate's default minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour 'timestamp-required' marks an
un-timestamped release pending -- so the hold never expires, at any soak length.
visibilityspots/cloudflared carries the identical 14-day soak and is exposed to the same
mechanism, but was NOT held at the time of writing: its tag last moved 199 days ago, so
the soak had already elapsed. Do not read its green state as evidence the hold is
harmless -- the next repoint restarts the clock.
Scope is deliberate and is the whole design decision here. It is repo-wide rather than a
list of the two deps observed, because every docker dep in this repo is digest-pinned
(docker:pinDigests is extended globally) and several sit on tags that are mutable by
construction ('latest', or no tag at all), so an allowlist would silently fail to protect
the next one added. It is restricted to matchDatasources 'docker' because there IS a case
where soaking a digest is wanted and must not be swept up: the github-actions SHA pins
(helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests), where ppat/renovate-presets soaks a repointed action tag
for 3 days if the publisher is trusted and 30 if not. That soak guards against a tag being
moved to hostile code, which is a real threat for a third-party action and not the
situation a rebuilt container image is in.
Version updates are untouched: this rule matches updateType 'digest' only, so an image's
own semver/calver soak still applies. 'pinDigest' (first-time pinning) is also untouched.
Ordering is load-bearing -- see the file note above.
